correctness.rationale: Normalize the regular \(N\)-gon, \(N=8k+4\), to Euclidean inradius \(1\). Then \(\|z\|_N\le\|z\|_2\) and every unit vector satisfies \(\|x\|_2\le\sec(\pi/N)\). For \(A=\|x+y\|_N\) and \(B=\|x-y\|_N\), the Euclidean parallelogram identity gives \(A^2+B^2\le4\sec^2(\pi/N)\), hence \(\min\{A,B\}\le\sqrt2\sec(\pi/N)\). Equality is explicit: because \((2k+1)/N=1/4\), the polygon has a vertex at angle \(\pi/4\); its quarter-turn is another vertex, while their sum and difference point along facet normals. Both polygonal norms therefore equal \(\sqrt2\sec(\pi/N)\).
risks: The script checks examples only; the universal quantifier over \(k\) is justified by the symbolic proof, not by computation.
The formula depends on regularity up to linear isometry; it is not asserted for arbitrary equiangular or centrally symmetric polygons.

value.rationale: The James constant is a standard quantitative measure of non-squareness, and the motivating source develops a vertex method precisely to make polyhedral examples computable. The theorem converts one residue class of all regular polygons into a closed exact family rather than another isolated table entry. The condition \(N\equiv4\pmod8\) is mathematically motivated by an exact vertex/facet alignment, and the octagonal counter-residue demonstrates that this structure is substantive. The dodecagonal value supplies the first nontrivial member and a natural benchmark for further regular-polygon comparisons.
risks: The theorem gives one infinite residue class, not a complete classification of James constants for all regular even polygons.
